options: The percentage of total GPU memory currently allocated
The ratio of active warps per SM to the maximum number of warps that SM supports
The number of kernels queued for execution
The clock speed of the SM relative to its rated maximum
questions.explain: Occupancy is active warps per SM divided by that SM's maximum supported warps — a measure of how fully the scheduler's warp slots are being used.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three resources that typically cap occupancy?
options: Registers per thread
Shared memory per block
Threads per block
The GPU's PCIe link generation
questions.explain: Occupancy is capped by registers per thread, shared memory per block, and threads per block — not by the PCIe link, which affects host-device transfer, not on-chip scheduling.

questions.q: Why does higher occupancy often help a memory-bound kernel's throughput?
options: More resident warps give the scheduler more options to hide a stalled warp's memory wait behind other warps' work
Higher occupancy always doubles the clock speed
It reduces the total number of bytes the kernel needs to read
It automatically enables Tensor Core execution
questions.explain: With more warps resident, the SM's scheduler has more ready-to-run warps to switch to while one warp waits on memory, hiding that latency.

options: The total GPU memory available
How many thread blocks of a given kernel/configuration can be resident on one SM at once
The number of SMs on the GPU
The current temperature of the GPU
questions.explain: This CUDA runtime API computes, for a specific kernel and block size, how many blocks can actually reside concurrently on a single SM.

questions.q: Why isn't maximizing occupancy to 100% always the best choice?
options: 100% occupancy is impossible to achieve on any GPU

A compute-bound kernel that already saturates its cores gains little from more resident warps, and using more registers per thread to avoid spilling can sometimes outperform packing in more warps at lower occupancy
Occupancy has no effect on performance at all
High occupancy always causes an out-of-memory error
questions.explain: Occupancy mainly helps hide memory latency. A compute-bound kernel isn't latency-limited, so pushing occupancy higher — sometimes at the cost of register spilling — may not help or could even hurt.
